rejected_findings.title: Invalid source filter shows all rows when mapping fails
rejected_findings.why_it_matters: When a workflow has a configuration error, the new source filter offers ‘Invalid rows only (0)’, but selecting it still displays every source row. The worker bypasses the selected filter whenever workflow issues exist, so the visible table contradicts its filter and count. Apply the filter against the available run rows even in this state; with no evaluated rows, the invalid and exception filters should show an empty result.

rejected_findings.title: Group identical calculation failures by source and rule
rejected_findings.why_it_matters: When two output fields use the same calculation over an invalid source operand, the exception review still shows two separate actionable items for one source/rule problem. For example, two identical Units × 2 recipes with Units=Twelve produce distinct cause keys solely because their output field IDs differ, so reviewIssues cannot combine their affected outputs. This leaves the flat duplicate presentation in place for calculation roots even though the new contract requires source/rule causes with affected output fields.

docs/plans/2026-10-11-1607-feat-operations-data-cleaner-plan.md:280 -- Engineering targets include single-row correction within 200 ms at the supported 10,000-by-20 scale.
rejected_findings.first_evidence: src/processing.worker.ts:112 --         const nextRun = correctedRun(workflow, source, next);
rejected_findings.suggested_fix: Generalize correctedRun's existing previous/changed-row path to accept the set of distinct edited row IDs: validate the candidate overlay, evaluate those rows, replace their results in the prior run, recount summary and csvRisk, and only then commit corrections/run/revision atomically. Fall back to full evaluation for a workflow change or workflow-level validation failure. Measure a 10,000-by-20 single-row correction as well as a multi-row batch.
rejected_findings.title: Single-cell batch reapplies every row
rejected_findings.why_it_matters: Applying even one staged correction now recomputes every row and output field before the corrected view appears. For the supported 10,000-row, 20-column workflow, correction latency therefore grows with the entire dataset rather than the number of touched rows, losing the prior incremental path and putting the documented 200 ms single-row target at risk. Evaluate the touched rows as one candidate batch, then publish the merged run only after all validation succeeds.
rejected_findings.reason: Rejected: full-dataset evaluation is the selected one-revalidation atomic batch design explicitly required by issue14/R8 and KTD2; source is evaluated in the worker before promotion. Reviewer established extra work but supplied no measured failed timing/responsiveness consequence at supported scale; current10kcorrection/browser checks are reported passing. Incremental batch optimization is an alternative mechanism, not a demonstrated defect.

rejected_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the requested field ID to MappingRows as a prop and let MappingRows set its existing editing state when that field is present and enabled. Clear the request after MappingRows handles it; delete the document query and synthetic button click in Workspace.
rejected_findings.title: Information Leakage: settings navigation depends on MappingRows markup
rejected_findings.why_it_matters: The exception action opens a field's settings by finding a MappingRows card through its CSS class and data attribute, then clicking that card's private edit button. Changing either component's markup or button state can silently break navigation, and the parent clears the target even if no button was found. MappingRows already owns the editing state, so a field-ID request can open the same dialog without coupling the parent to its DOM structure.
rejected_findings.reason: Rejected: current code demonstrably locates the existing data-field-id/edit controls in MappingRows and triggers the existing settings state. tests/e2e/acceptance-corrections.spec.ts rule-failures journey exercises the requested navigation. Replacing it with a prop may be an alternative structure, but no present broken behavior or worthwhile maintenance benefit sufficient to justify disruption was established.
